oracle.tool: tools/c-oracle (libclang, verdict from clang's own diagnostic categories)
oracle.note: THREE-VALUED: valid / invalid / indeterminate, the only oracle that is. See crates/treebank-c/ORACLE.md; the claim is 'no syntax error, in GNU C, given these include paths', NOT 'this compiles'. Lang::validate collapses indeterminate to false, so gap_files is a FLOOR. This is the language that proves `flags` has to exist: -std=gnu17 selects the dialect and the libclang version alone does not settle it. The include-path flags are per-file and are described in corpus.oracle_flags rather than here.

corpus.source: Debian sid, source packages ranked by popcon (popularity-contest) installs aggregated per source package, filtered to packages whose sources.debian.org SLOC is >=2000 ansic and ansic >= cpp; upstream .orig.tar.* only (never the .debian.tar.* patch tarball); .c and .h files, C++ headers excluded by content
corpus.source_note: C has no registry, so popularity is borrowed. popcon counts machines, which is closer in kind to crates.io downloads than Java's dependent-repos proxy. The bias is explicit and it is the point: this corpus is the C that ships in a distribution — system libraries, daemons, autotools trees, GNU extensions — NOT trending C on GitHub, which is a different corpus and would give different gap numbers. The SLOC filter exists because popcon ranks everything Debian ships: without it the top of the list spends its bandwidth on LibreOffice (4.4M lines of C++ to 34k of C) and gcc-16 (no C at all).
corpus.oracle: tools/c-oracle — libclang 20.1.2, parse-only, verdict from clang's own diagnostic categories. THREE-VALUED: valid / invalid / indeterminate. See crates/treebank-c/ORACLE.md for what it does and does not claim; the short version is 'no syntax error, in GNU C, given these include paths', NOT 'this compiles'. Lang::validate collapses indeterminate to false, so gap_files is a FLOOR and noise_files mixes 'reference rejected it' with 'could not tell'; the full split is in corpus/c/oracle-verdicts.json and on the sweep's stderr.
corpus.fetched: 2026-08-08 (popcon + sid Sources snapshot of that date)
corpus.files_note: .c and .h from the top 20 C source packages by popcon; 365 of 12,767 headers dropped as C++ (unguarded namespace/template/class, comments and __cplusplus-guarded regions excluded from the scan)

oracle_split.note: of the 17,937 failing files. INDETERMINATE OUTNUMBERS VALID 2.2:1, so gap_files is a floor and noise_files (12,435) mixes 'reference rejected it' (452) with 'could not tell' (11,983). ~79% of indeterminates carry an unresolved include; the largest remaining class is the configure-generated config.h, which no static include path can supply.

corpus.oracle_flags: -std=gnu17 -ferror-limit=0 -w, -iquote<every header-bearing dir in the package and its ancestors>, -I<package root, include/, inc/, src/, lib/>, -idirafter<every header-bearing dir>
corpus.oracle_flags_note: Three search paths, each doing a distinct job. -iquote answers the package's own quoted includes. -I is limited to the package's PUBLIC dirs on purpose: it is searched before the system dirs, so a wide -I list lets a package's private replacements for system headers shadow the real ones (glibc string/string.h answering <string.h>) and resolution gets WORSE (measured: 4578 -> 4060 valid). -idirafter carries the wide list instead; being searched AFTER the system dirs it can only supply headers the system lacks, which is what glibc's <sigsetops.h> needs. Measured on 1,500 failing files: -iquote+public -I alone = 372 valid / 11 invalid / 1117 indeterminate; adding -idirafter = 453 / 37 / 1010.

top_gap_clusters.class: statement macro followed by a block, e.g. list_for_each(li, &q->ifaces) { ... }
extern "C" brace asymmetry: `{` inside one #ifdef __cplusplus and `}` inside another. Preprocessor-inherent, same shape as the C# asymmetry; not a fixable grammar bug
undefined macro in declaration position, e.g. _INLINE_ void __list_add(...)
macro in declaration position, e.g. THREAD_LOCAL int adjustment = 0;
type as a macro argument, e.g. list_entry(a, struct file_element, file_list)

corpus.oracle_correction: The first published numbers for this corpus (gap 5629, invalid 302, indeterminate 12006) were computed while c-oracle had a fixed 128-flag cap per request, which silently truncated the include list for the three largest packages — glibc alone has 498 header-bearing dirs. The cap is gone; the numbers above are the corrected ones. The truncation also made -idirafter look inert, because its flags were the ones being dropped.
corpus.source_freshness: rank re-downloads the sid Sources index when the cached copy is older than 12h (TREEBANK_REFRESH_SOURCES=1 forces it). The index carries every package's version, so a permanently cached copy froze the corpus: resolve() would return the same tarballs forever, the sweep cache would skip them all, and the 'new version of a top-K package' event this loop is built on could never fire for C. The per-package SLOC verdicts are cached in corpus/c/db/sloc.json keyed by name and stamped with the version measured, so a daily re-rank queries only the packages whose version moved — measured at k=200: 227 lookups in 9s cold (~25/sec, 8-way), then 2 lookups and 1.9s warm. sources.debian.org lags the archive, so a version it has not indexed yet falls back to the newest it does hold; without that, a refresh on an upload day silently dropped glibc and mesa, the two largest C sources in the corpus.
corpus.preprocessing: crates/treebank-preprocessing, declared via Lang::preprocessing(): __cplusplus is undefined when parsing C. The sweep re-parses each VALID failing file with dead branches removed; the 909 that then parse cleanly are recorded as config_files rather than gaps, because no grammar patch can fix them — a header opening `extern "C" {` inside one #ifdef __cplusplus and closing `}` inside another has no single well-formed tree. Without this they sat at #2 in the fix queue, the largest cluster an agent could not win. A second pass forces individual conditional branches: where the symbol is unknown (#ifdef F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC around one of two spellings of a signature) it does not matter what the symbol means, because both branches are valid and the grammar fails only on seeing both. 51 more files are explained entirely this way and 43 are re-clustered onto the problem that was hiding behind a split. The soundness guard is that the error's own line must survive the forcing — without it an include guard 'clears' every error in a header by emptying it, which accounted for 173 of 243 raw hits.
corpus.macro_diagnosis: crates/treebank-preprocessing expands the package's macros into each gap file and re-parses. 1,102 of the 4,593 gap files (24.0%) then parse cleanly, so the grammar was meeting an unexpanded macro rather than unfamiliar syntax. This does NOT change the verdict — unlike the extern "C" case, THREAD_LOCAL int x; is something a grammar could parse — it annotates each cluster with the macros responsible (SPA_EXPORT, drm_public, _PUBLIC_, DBUS_EXPORT, NCURSES_CONST, weak_alias...), which is what writing a minimal rule and judging its over-acceptance needs.
